name: NAR REACH: the National Association of REALTORS® technology scale-up program page
title: NAR REACH: the National Association of REALTORS® technology scale-up program page
answer: This is the National Association of REALTORS® landing page for REACH, described as a technology scale-up program created by Second Century Ventures, which the page calls the most active venture fund in the global real estate technology space. That single sentence is the page's only substantive claim about the program. The rest of the harvested text is site navigation, menus and general NAR member resources, so the page names REACH and its parent fund but gives no detail on how the program works, which companies it backs or when.

sections.body: The page is published by the National Association of REALTORS® on nar.realtor and is a landing page for REACH, a technology scale-up program. It sits within NAR's wider site, alongside menus for member resources, training, news and policy. The harvested text states no publication date and no author. Its scope is limited to introducing REACH and pointing visitors to the rest of NAR's site, so it functions as an entry point rather than a report or an article.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The substantive content is a single repeated sentence: REACH is a unique technology scale-up program created by Second Century Ventures, the most active venture fund in the global real estate technology space. The sentence appears twice in the harvested text, once at the top and once immediately after. Everything else on the page is navigation and promotional copy for the wider NAR site. Those menus describe NAR as an American trade association involved in all aspects of residential and commercial real estate, and they point to resources for new agents and experienced brokers, home buying and selling, commercial and international business, member information and technology. Other menu items cover data and statistics for improving a business, training through NAR's affiliated Institutes, Societies and Councils, daily industry news and events, designations and certifications, trademark rules stating that only NAR members may call themselves REALTORS®, and the REALTORS® Political Action Committee, which promotes the election of pro-REALTOR® candidates across the United States. The page also mentions MLSs, brokers, buyers and sellers in connection with NAR policy updates. No detail is given about how REACH selects or supports companies, which companies it has backed, how long it runs or what it costs.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, dates or funding figures. The claims it does make are attributed to the page itself: that REACH is a unique technology scale-up program, that it was created by Second Century Ventures, and that Second Century Ventures is the most active venture fund in the global real estate technology space. It also states that only members of NAR can call themselves a REALTOR®, and that NAR is an American trade association involved in all aspects of residential and commercial real estate.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader tracking AI in real estate would use this page only to confirm what REACH is and who runs it, namely a scale-up program from Second Century Ventures, the venture arm described here as the most active in global real estate technology. It establishes the accelerator's identity and its link to NAR, which is useful for citing the program as a place where residential proptech gets vetted. It does not, however, name any participating company, describe any technology, or mention artificial intelligence at all, so it cannot support claims about which AI tools the profession is adopting.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: The page is a commercial and promotional landing page for NAR and its venture program, not an independent or research document. It carries no date, no author and no methodology. It gives no list of portfolio companies, no selection criteria, no outcomes and no mention of artificial intelligence. Because the harvested text is mostly repeated navigation, it is thin even as a description of REACH, and any claim about the program's role in AI adoption would need a different source.
